video_title: Why The Future Of NBA Europe Is UNCERTAIN: Latest Updates Explained

quotes.speaker: Aris Barkas
quotes.summary_phrase: EuroLeague's origins as a private league established in 2001
quotes.excerpt: EuroLeague, which is a private league. It was established back in 2001.
quotes.quote: We have the top level which is the EuroLeague, which is a private league. It was established back in 2001. The big clubs decided that FIBA was not at the time ready to create a fully professional league that covered their needs, and they decided to create one for themselves. Those clubs are also competing in the domestic leagues, but in order to qualify for the EuroLeague, you have to have either a permanent spot, you may get a wild card depending the year, and also you can qualify by the EuroCup, which is the second tier of the EuroLeague.

quotes.speaker: Aris Barkas
quotes.summary_phrase: EuroLeague team composition and the shift toward franchise licenses
quotes.excerpt: EuroLeague is now transforming the licenses to franchises.
quotes.quote: In a league of 20 teams, 13 are shareholders, they have permanent licenses. But first of all, out of those 13 teams, there is CSKA Moscow, which due to the war in Ukraine, cannot play, but they remain shareholders. And also, we have to take into account the fact that EuroLeague is now transforming the licenses to franchises, probably because of NBA Europe.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA's potential hybrid model for European expansion
quotes.excerpt: The NBA is intending to go forward with this NBA Europe to start, they say in 2027.
quotes.quote: The NBA is intending to go forward with this NBA Europe to start, they say in 2027. I'll believe that when they actually say it and it starts. That's a lot to do in a year, but in theory, it could start in a year. And basically, the NBA and the EuroLeague are both in, and you mentioned Chus Bueno, who is the new CEO, who was a part of the NBA ecosystem until recently. He has basically said, I am open to working with the NBA, but we could go it alone. And Adam Silver and Mark Tatum have basically said the same thing, we could work with EuroLeague or we could go it alone.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA's proposed hybrid model for European expansion
quotes.excerpt: They want a hybrid model, and a hybrid model means that they will have permanent teams.
quotes.quote: They want a hybrid model, and a hybrid model means that they will have permanent teams that will never leave the top league of NBA Europe, just like EuroLeague has. 12 permanent franchises is what they envision at least to start. And then there would be four teams that could move in and out of NBA Europe, so this league would have relegation, but not for the permanent teams, just for those four teams. And it would be for one year. You'd get in for one year.

quotes.speaker: Aris Barkas
quotes.summary_phrase: FIBA's condition for cooperation with the NBA
quotes.excerpt: FIBA has one condition in the cooperation with the NBA, and this is that 25% of the new European league.
quotes.quote: FIBA has one condition in the cooperation with the NBA, and this is that 25% of the new European league, of NBA Europe, will be always open for qualification, because this is essentially the European model. Right now, this means four spots out of 16. So the finalist and the winner of the BCL, of the Basketball Champions League, will qualify for the inaugural NBA Europe season.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA's financial projections for European team valuations
quotes.excerpt: The NBA is saying that they think that they will get between 500 and a billion dollars.
quotes.quote: The NBA is saying that they think that they will get between 500 and a billion dollars for some of these teams. Some people think that that's a laughable number, but they say that they have 12 spots and that they have offers on all 12 of those spots.

quotes.speaker: Aris Barkas
quotes.excerpt: The newest unconfirmed information is that the London bid can end up being 1.5 billion.
quotes.quote: The newest unconfirmed information is that the London bid can end up being 1.5 billion.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA's strategy to reinvest expansion revenue into European clubs
quotes.excerpt: They will use this money to invest in each of these clubs down to the youth level.
quotes.quote: They will use this money to invest in each of these clubs down to the youth level. That this money will largely be redirected back to investing, because this is a long-term project and they want to invest in the infrastructure of each team to build from the ground up. Again, this is what they say. It sounds altruistic, who knows how true it is, but this is their position.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Calangelo's involvement with a new European team
quotes.excerpt: Brian Colangelo, former two-time Executive of the Year in Phoenix and Toronto, will be a part of this team.
quotes.quote: Just this week it came out that Brian Colangelo, former two-time Executive of the Year in Phoenix and Toronto, obviously was a GM in Philly, he will be a part of this team.

quotes.speaker: Aris Barkas
quotes.summary_phrase: Francesco Totti's involvement with the Maxima Roma project
quotes.excerpt: Francesco Totti, he's let's say a god in Rome.
quotes.quote: First of all, it's Totti. Secondly, he's let's say a god in Rome. For Rome, he's much more important than Messi. He's the Maradona of Rome, let's put it like this.
